chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Ja'fari, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
A food-spread is not fruitful (beneficial) without salt upon it, and it is more corrective for the body that one begins with it at the start of the meal.
ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of eating salt at the beginning of a meal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) links the physical preservation of food ('khusb') to the spiritual and communal value of salt, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *tibb* (prophetic medicine) as a means of maintaining bodily health for worship. The instruction to begin with salt underscores the principle of *ibtida'* (starting with the best) in daily sustenance, aligning physical well-being with spiritual discipline. This narration is often cited by Shia scholars to demonstrate the integration of practical hygiene and dietary wisdom within the Imams' teachings.
